title: Fix project binding race during API key rebind that causes quota attribution to flip-flop across workspaces
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: A race condition during API key rebinding (when migrating or reassigning an API key between projects/subaccounts) leads to a window where incoming requests are stamped with the wrong project/org for billing and quota enforcement. Customers reported intermittent quota errors and unexpected usage billed to the wrong project after a key rebind operation.

Symptoms observed: interleaved requests in logs where identical request IDs are attributed first to project A then to project B within seconds; sporadic rate limiter owner mismatches; billing dashboard spikes for projects that should have had zero traffic during the rebind window.

Why this matters: misattributed tokens cause incorrect quotas, throttling on the wrong projects, and potential billing disputes. This undermines the Dedicated/Private customer guarantees and can escalate to enterprise support incidents.

Related artifacts:
- Incident timeline and initial signal: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/billing/tenant-attribution-ops?orgId=1 (internal)
- Sentry event sample: https://sentry.redwood.internal/issue/RE-8081
- Initial support case: CUST-2026-1892 (Customer: FinchHealth)
repro_steps: 1) Create an API key bound to workspace/project A and generate sustained traffic (burst of small requests).
2) In a separate transaction, rebind the API key to workspace/project B (this is done via token-rebind job that creates new mapping and deletes the old mapping).
3) During the rebind window, send additional requests using the same API key and observe attribution headers and rate-limiter owner stamp in the request logs.
4) Observe that some requests are attributed to A and some to B within a short timeframe; rate-limiter buckets and billing counters reflect both attributions.
observed_evidence: Log excerpt (auth-service): owner_lookup=cache_hit project=A ttl=3s then owner_lookup=stale project=B immediately after alias-swap
Rate-limiter metrics: rate_limiter.owner_change_count spiked during rebind (see Grafana dashboard above)
Billing increment delta in invoice snapshot: project B shows non-zero token counts during the rebind window
root_cause_analysis: Race between async token-rebind job (which updates the token->project mapping in Postgres) and the in-memory attribution cache used by the API gateway. The cache TTL and an out-of-order cache priming path allow stale mapping to survive briefly after the DB swap.

Rate-limiter owner assignment reads the cached mapping instead of consulting the authoritative DB when the cache reports a miss under heavy concurrency, causing split attribution during a small window.
No atomic handover semantics exist for rebind operations: the system performs delete + insert semantics across multiple services instead of an atomic pointer swap that consumers can consult.
mitigation_applied: Emergency mitigation (2026-03-06): increased cache TTL to 30s to reduce flip-flop frequency and paused automated token-rebinds for scheduled migrations.

Support mitigation: ran a reconciliation script to attribute traffic in the 6-hour window to the correct owner using request logs and token snapshotting: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Token+Rebind+Reconciliation
Operational change: added a temporary block in the UI preventing simultaneous rebinds of the same token across projects until fix is deployed.
fix_plan: 1) Implement atomic token aliasing in the tenant graph: add a single authoritative token_alias table record that points to a project_id and is updated with a single DB transaction + versioned tombstone.

2) Update attribution path: gateway and rate-limiter should consult token_alias with a fast read-through cache that supports conditional GET by version; on mismatch, fall back to DB and prime cache with the version to avoid flip-flop.

3) Add transactional swap endpoint in control-plane: token_rebind.swap(token_id, new_project_id) that emits a single change event with version metadata consumed by services via a lightweight streaming channel (kafka topic).
4) Ensure rate-limiter owner assignment is deterministic by reading versioned mapping; make owner assignment idempotent and tolerant to replays.
5) Backfill reconciliation job to correct historical misattributions for the last 30 days using signed request logs and token snapshots.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for token_alias swap semantics and versioned cache priming.
Integration test that simulates concurrent rebind and high-throughput requests; verify 0% split-attribution across 10k requests.
Chaos test during canary: run rebinds under network partitions and ensure system either fully attributes to old or new owner, never both.
E2E billing smoke test against staging billing pipeline to ensure invoice counters align with request logs after swap.
deployment_and_rollout: Phase 1 (canary, 1-2 hosts): roll out atomic aliasing and gateway cache versioning to canary: runtime-1.26/canary
Phase 2 (limited region): enable swap endpoint for non-critical customers and run simulated rebinds overnight
Phase 3 (full rollout): enable for all control-plane clusters, open UI rebind, and monitor rate_limiter.owner_change_count and billing drift dashboards for 72h
Rollback plan: revert to paused rebinds and restore previous cache TTL if customer-facing regressions detected
post_deploy_metrics: target: rate_limiter.owner_change_count down to baseline within 5 minutes of swap
monitor: billing_delta_by_project for unexpected token increments in next 7 days
reconciliation_tasks: Write and run backfill job: scripts/reconcile_token_attribution.py (PR: https://github.com/redwood/reconciliation/pull/142)
Export affected request windows to S3 and produce corrected usage CSVs for billing: s3://redwood-internal/rebind-reconciliation/2026-03
Coordinate with finance to apply corrective billing adjustments for impacted customers (list attached to support ticket CUST-2026-1892)
comments: 2026-03-05 - Ava Thompson: Created ticket after support case from FinchHealth reported 3 misattributed invoices. Initial logs show owner flip-flop during scheduled token migration.
2026-03-06 - Ravi Patel: Deployed cache TTL increase as an emergency mitigation. Started drafting atomic aliasing design doc.
2026-03-08 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Verified that rate_limiter.owner_change_count spike correlates with rebind cron at 02:00 UTC. Recommend transactional swap to avoid race.
2026-03-10 - PM (Omar Ruiz): Noted customer impact as medium; asked to prioritize for runtime-1.26. Finance requested a list of affected customers for remediation.
2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: WIP on PR for control-plane swap API; gateway changes under code review (PR links above). Added integration test harness.
2026-03-12 - Design review: agreed on versioned token_alias table and streaming change events. Deferred KMS changes to follow-up.
notes: Edge case: if a customer performs multiple rapid rebinds, reconciliation may require combining multiple snapshots; reconciliation job will prefer last-writer-by-version semantics.
Longer-term: consider exposing token binding telemetry to customers (audit logs) to reduce friction on disputes.
